requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
**Verdict: true.** The code implements each obligation in the requirement, and tests cover the main design cases. I read the supplied source snippets and tests. I did not search the rest of the repository.

**Location and creation**
- `UsageLog::start` (`src/authoring/usage.rs`) creates `<state>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` with `create_dir_all`. It uses a run id built from nanosecond time, process id and a sequence counter, and opens the file with `create_new`. Each assessment therefore gets its own file.
- `author_evidence_with_output` and `prepare_assessment` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) take the state root from `config::state_root()`. It resolves `$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas`, `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`, and returns an error if none can be determined. The caller propagates that error, so no history is claimed.
- Both functions create the state directory. They refuse to run if the canonicalized state directory lies inside the project root, so usage stays outside the project in stdout mode and in file mode.
- `tests/configuration.rs` checks the state-root resolution for Unix and Windows, including invalid XDG values and missing variables.

**Record contents**
- The record struct (`src/authoring/usage.rs`) holds `version` (1), `run_id`, `project_root`, `subject`, `subject_kind`, `backend`, `model`, `start_time_ms`, `end_time_ms`, `outcome`, `determination`, `evidence_output` and `evidence_written`.
- Backend, model and subject kind are filled in as they become known (`configured_record`). The determination kind comes from `Judgment::kind()`, which returns only `"true"`, `"false"` or `"FIXME"`. FIXME entry text is never stored. `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` asserts that `#125` and the rationale text do not appear in the usage record.
- `evidence_output` is set to `file` or `stdout` and saved before the work starts. `evidence_written` is set to true after a successful write to either destination (`configured_assessment`, `PendingAssessment::persisted`).
- `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` asserts `evidence_output == "stdout"` and `evidence_written == true` for true, false and FIXME judgments.
- `live_bedrock_authoring` makes the same assertions against a real Bedrock backend, but it is skipped under `CI`, so it adds coverage only when run locally with credentials.

**Distinguishing outcomes**
- A new record starts as `"unfinished"` with no end time. `finish` sets `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled` together with the end time. Ctrl-C and interruption map to `cancelled`.
- `cancelled_request_persists_elapsed_time_and_incomplete_totals` checks the unfinished, then cancelled states. `missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence` checks `failed` with `evidence_written == false` in both output modes.
- `failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage` covers an accepted judgment whose evidence write fails. The record shows `failed`, determination `FIXME` and `evidence_written == false`.
- The batch tests cover completed, failed and denied-read runs, with one usage record per subject.

**No source, prompts, responses or rationale**
- `input_metadata_counts_components_and_reads_without_persisting_source` asserts that source text and file names do not appear in the usage file.
- `tool_outcomes_are_distinct_and_unknown_names_do_not_leak_model_text` shows that unknown tool names are recorded as "unknown".
- The CLI test checks that the requirement, definition, source and rationale secrets are absent. `authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file` checks that a literal API key is absent.

**Persistence failures**
- If usage cannot be recorded, the error is surfaced and mentions the usage path and whether evidence was written (`finish` error mapping, `persisted`, `failed`). Nothing claims the history was recorded when it was not.

**Minor gaps, not enough to fail**
- `subject_kind` can be absent if a run fails before the sources are prepared. The requirement says to record backend and model "when known" and lists the subject kind unconditionally, so this is a narrow edge case.
- No test exercises a state directory inside the project or an unwritable state directory. Both paths are simple, direct error returns.
- There are no FIXME markers for this requirement in the supplied sources.

Rust-item selectors use syntactic ancestry within one repository-relative file. Examples include `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, and positional `use#1`. Duplicate sibling names gain `#1`, `#2`, and so on. Delimiter characters and whitespace within names or impl types use percent-encoded UTF-8 bytes, so spelling can be recovered without resolving modules across files. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`

This determination assesses citation coverage; FIXME applies to requirement and example judgments. It needs one Rust-item input for that function and at least one requirements input covering every cited definition. The agent must review the whole function and relevant definitions, then explain why its citations include *every applicable* requirement or named example and how those texts account for its behavior together.
